title: F_5 and F_7 cross-validation vs external CAS
description: Cross-validate `permanent_bipedal5` (T18) and `permanent_bipedal7` (T20) against an external computer algebra system (Sage or Magma) on a small test-vector suite, generated offline and committed. ## Background The in-tree oracle (`permanent_ryser>`, T7) is sufficient for the epic's `[hard]` correctness criterion — but agreement with an external CAS gives independent confidence that even the oracle is right. Sage's `Matrix.permanent()` over `GF(5)` and `GF(7)` is the canonical second opinion. This issue commits a CAS-generated test vector file at `crates/gf2-algebra/tests/data/cas_permanent_f5_f7.csv` (rows: `q, n, matrix_serialised, expected_permanent`) and an integration test that consumes it. The CSV is generated offline by a Sage script committed at `scripts/generate-cas-permanent-vectors.sage`; the script's reproducibility is verified manually before the data is committed. ## Success Criteria - [ ] [hard] `crates/gf2-algebra/tests/data/cas_permanent_f5_f7.csv` exists with at least 100 vectors per $(q, n)$ cell for $q \in \{5, 7\}$ and $n \in \{4, 6, 8, 10, 12\}$. - [ ] [hard] `crates/gf2-algebra/tests/cas_cross_validation.rs` integration test reads the CSV and checks `permanent_bipedal5` / `permanent_bipedal7` match the CAS-recorded value bit-for-bit on every vector. - [ ] [hard] `scripts/generate-cas-permanent-vectors.sage` exists, is documented, and was run with a fixed RNG seed; running it again produces the same CSV. - [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes.
